Plausible values: keep the scoring basis with the draws

Source: vignettes/articles/application-plausible-values.Rmd
application-plausible-values.Rmd

One posterior mean gives one summary per Person. Repeated posterior draws retain variation around that summary and can be useful in later analyses. The draws must travel with their IDs, scoring basis and limitations: exporting numbers alone does not establish a valid population analysis.

This short example starts from the package’s saved synthetic JML calibration, scores two invented Persons, and saves the resulting object. It demonstrates conditional posterior scoring and data handoff, not a survey regression or a population-level uncertainty guarantee. No external survey package is needed.

Draw values from a stated scoring model

Show R code: load the calibration and score two new Persons 
library(mfrmr)
example <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example$fit
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data(example$dataset)

# Invented responses using levels present in the saved calibration.
new_ratings <- data.frame(
  Person = rep(c("NEW01", "NEW02"), each = 2),
  Rater = as.character(unique(ratings$Rater)[1]),
  Criterion = rep(as.character(unique(ratings$Criterion)[1:2]), 2),
  Score = c(2, 3, 1, 2)
)
pv <- sample_mfrm_plausible_values(
  fit, new_ratings, n_draws = 20, seed = 23
)

The source fit is JML. This scoring step adds the package’s standard-normal reference prior while keeping the fitted facet/step calibration fixed. The prior is an assumption for posterior scoring; JML has not estimated a Person population distribution. For supported MML fits, the default instead uses the fitted population, including Person covariates when specified.

Person Draw Value CalibrationMethod
NEW01 1 -0.560 JML
NEW01 2 0.000 JML
NEW01 3 -0.560 JML
NEW01 4 0.560 JML
NEW01 5 -1.121 JML
NEW01 6 -0.560 JML

The same Person appears once per draw. Twenty draws do not turn two Persons into forty independent observations. Values are sampled from the fitted quadrature-grid posterior; repetitions of a value are expected.

Inspect the numerical review and retain its meaning

Show R code: inspect summaries, settings and review information 
draw_summary <- summary(pv)$draw_summary
draw_summary[c("Person", "Draws", "MeanValue", "SDValue")]
pv$settings[c("method", "posterior_basis", "scoring_quad_points", "seed")]
pv$row_review
pv$population_review
pv$notes
Person Draws MeanValue SDValue
NEW01 20 -0.533 0.864
NEW02 20 -1.180 0.705

These are summaries of a finite set of draws. With twenty draws, the empirical mean, SD and quantiles have appreciable Monte Carlo variation. The companion pv$estimates table contains the posterior scoring summaries computed from the quadrature rule. Increasing the number of draws can reduce simulation error; it does not supply missing conditioning variables or calibration uncertainty.

Save the complete object before reshaping

Show R code: save, reload and split into one table per draw 
# Choose a private location for real Person data.
local_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mfrmr-pv-example")
dir.create(local_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(pv, file.path(local_dir, "plausible-values.rds"))
restored <- readRDS(file.path(local_dir, "plausible-values.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(pv, restored))

by_draw <- split(restored$values, restored$values$Draw)
stopifnot(all(vapply(by_draw, function(x) !anyDuplicated(x$Person), logical(1))))

The RDS retains the scoring settings, fit identity, review tables and notes. Each by_draw table can be joined to a Person-level background/design table by ID for a downstream analysis. Check missing, duplicate and unmatched IDs before joining. Keep the full object even if a receiving tool needs a wide matrix or a smaller set of columns. For an analysis bundle with its source fit, see export_mfrm_bundle().

Choose the downstream analysis separately

Intended use What remains to justify
Describe these conditional draws Their scoring prior, calibration, numerical review and finite-draw approximation.
Estimate a population mean or regression A conditioning model compatible with that analysis, the target population, sampling design and an appropriate uncertainty-combination rule. The two-Person example does not establish these.
Use official IEA plausible values Follow that survey’s PV and sampling documentation directly; no mfrmr recalibration is required.

BIFIEsurvey’s data interface and EdSurvey’s survey objects are possible downstream routes. This page does not claim a tested adapter to either package. Use their documented analysis workflow when it matches the question, and verify the within-PV, between-PV and combined variance for that workflow. Rating weights, sampling weights and replicate weights have distinct roles. An ordinary regression on averaged PVs or on all draws stacked as independent people does not perform that uncertainty propagation.

Calibration and fitted population parameters remain fixed in the current draws. A downstream variance calculation does not automatically add their estimation uncertainty. See sample_mfrm_plausible_values() for supported models and scoring options. Independent downstream code can use these outputs without a new mfrmr API or an IEA-specific workflow.
